Brief: Tell me about Alan Turing and elaborate on the impact of his work. — about University and work on computability

1. In 1929 Turing and his friend Christopher Morcom applied for scholarships at Trinity College, Cambridge.
2. Morcom, who was successful, had various advantages over Turing – he was nearly a year older, and both his father and brother had studied at Trinity.
3. However, he died three months after the offer was made.
4. Turing, on the other hand, was unsuccessful, but sat the King's College, Cambridge Scholarship Examination in Mathematics in 1930.
5. King's reserved most of its places for Etonians (there was a historic link with Eton as a feeder institution), making the exam very competitive for candidates from other schools.
6. However, its examiners had a slightly different slant to those in other colleges.
7. Hodges describes the King's examiners as looking for "a spark of originality" and notes that the papers were "notorious for their unorthodox questions".
8. Turing was awarded an exhibition (a lower-value scholarship) worth £80 per annum (equivalent to about £4,300 as of 2023).
9. His undergraduate studies at Cambridge were from February 1931 to November 1934.
10. He studied "Schedule B" of the Mathematical Tripos course.
11. He was awarded first-class honours in mathematics.
12. It was finally accepted on 16 March 1935.
